title: Srivijaya
summary: Srivijaya was a Buddhist maritime power based around Palembang on the Musi River in southeastern Sumatra. It is known from Old Malay inscriptions of the late 7th century and from Chinese records, and is described as flourishing from the 7th to the 13th century on control of sea trade. Whether it was a unified empire or a network of allied ports is debated.

uncertainty.note: Start is the earliest dated inscription (Kedukan Bukit, read as 682 or 683 CE), not a founding date. End is the loose 13th-century range given by one source. The polity may have begun earlier and faded rather than ended on one date.

as_recorded.value: The Kedukan Bukit inscription (dated to 683 CE) is the earliest known reference to Srivijaya.
Kedukan Bukit stone is dated about four years earlier than Kota Kapur (Saka 608, 686 CE).
Srivijaya was active in the 7th to 13th centuries CE.

where.historical_name: Srivijaya (Old Malay inscriptions), centred on the Musi River near Palembang

importance.justification: The leading Sumatran sea power of its era, linking Indian Ocean and China trade and sustaining Mahayana Buddhist learning.

sources.title: Srivijaya: A Buddhist maritime empire in Southeast Asia

reviewer_note: Least sure of dates and of the capital: 682 versus 683 for Kedukan Bukit, the end date (a loose 13th-century range), and whether the centre was always Palembang. Both opened sources are informal (a science blog and a museum volunteer site); a scholarly source (Coedes, Manguin) should replace them on expansion.
